user_prompt: What is the effect of exercise, compared with no treatment, usual care, or limited education, on quality of life at 12-month follow-up (sustainability of effect) in adults with knee osteoarthritis?  This is specifically the LONGER-TERM follow-up (up to and including 12 months post-intervention) — do not include quality-of-life data measured immediately at the end of the intervention period; that is a separate, earlier timepoint in this review.  The comparator is no treatment, usual care, or limited/minimal education — NOT an attention-control/placebo condition, and NOT a co-intervention comparison (i.e. do not include trials where exercise was added on top of another treatment and compared to that treatment alone — those are two separate comparisons in this review).  For quality of life, each study may report several outcome measures — identify whichever specific instrument the paper itself frames as its quality-of-life outcome (check its own methods/outcomes description), rather than defaulting to the first similarly-named score in a results table. Pool this as a standardized mean difference, since different studies use different specific instruments/scales for this construct.
